attrs.title: Merchant Center problems we fix
attrs.lead: The notices we see most often. The email names a policy, but rarely the exact problem.

items.title: Suspended for misrepresentation
items.text:
The most common suspension. Google thinks shoppers could be misled: no address or phone number, unclear returns, hidden costs, or offers it can’t verify. It applies to the whole account, so every product stops showing.

We check the store the way a Google reviewer would: contact page, about page, policies, checkout and offers. Our developers fix what’s missing, and we only request a review once everything is in place.

items.title: Website needs improvement
items.text:
Google says your site isn’t ready: pages under construction, broken links, placeholder text, or products you can’t actually buy. Sometimes it’s a new store that went live too early.

We go through the store page by page, remove placeholder text and dead links, make sure every product in the feed can be added to the cart, and test checkout on desktop and phone.

items.title: Prices or stock don’t match
items.text:
When the feed says one price and the site says another, Google warns you first. If it keeps happening, the account can be suspended for inaccurate product data.

We sync the feed with the store several times a day, handle sale prices with dates, and add structured data to product pages so Google reads the right price and stock.

items.title: Offers that look too good to be true
items.text:
Permanent “70% off” banners, “was” prices that were never charged, or claims like “original” and “certified” without proof. Google reads these as misleading.

We make every offer honest and easy to check: real sale dates, “was” prices you actually charged, and claims removed or backed up with evidence.

items.title: Products that break Shopping policies
items.text:
Some products can’t be advertised at all, and some only with rules: supplements with health claims, replicas, weapons, or adult products. One wrong product can flag the account.

We check the range against Google’s Shopping policies, remove or exclude products that can’t be shown, and rewrite titles and descriptions that make claims Google doesn’t allow.

items.title: A review request already refused
items.text:
Asking for a review without changing anything usually ends in a quick refusal. After that, Google can make you wait days before you can ask again.

We find out why the first request failed, fix everything we find, and send one review request with the changes in place. While you wait, we keep the store ready.

attrs.html:
What happens after you contact us

First a call, then five steps. Fast, careful and honest about the outcome.

A call back within 24 hours

Send us the suspension notice. A feed specialist calls you back within one working day to go through it with you, before any work starts.

  • A real person
  • No obligation
  • Plain English

  1. We read the suspension notice, your account history and any earlier review requests, then check your store and feed the way a Google reviewer would.

    You get: A clear picture of what Google is likely seeing.

    • The notice and the policy named
    • Account history and earlier review requests
    • Store checked page by page
    • Feed diagnostics and product data

  2. We tell you the most likely cause in plain English, what needs to change, who changes it and how strong your case is.

    You get: Written findings within 48 hours.

    • The most likely cause, and why we think so
    • A fix list in order of importance
    • Who makes each change: us or your team
    • An honest view of your chances

  3. Our developers update the store and our feed specialist fixes the product data: business details, policies, offers, prices, stock and restricted products.

    You get: Every change logged with before and after screenshots.

    • Contact, about and policy pages
    • Offers and claims made honest
    • Feed and store synced, with structured data
    • Restricted products excluded or rewritten

  4. Once everything is fixed, we request a review from your account, with you. One request, sent properly.

    You get: A review request with nothing left to fix.

    • Final check of store and feed
    • Review requested in Merchant Center
    • A note of every change for your records
    • The store kept ready while Google checks

  5. We watch for Google’s reply, check products as they come back, and if the answer is no, give you a clear plan for what to do next.

    You get: A plan either way.

    • Products checked as they’re reapproved
    • Diagnostics checked every week for 30 days
    • A plan B if the review fails
    • Tips to avoid another suspension

What we check

Eight things Google checks, checked and fixed

For each one: why it matters, what we check, what we often find and what we change.

Area 1 of 8

Business details and contact

Google wants to know who runs the store and how shoppers can reach you. Missing details are the most common cause of a misrepresentation suspension.

What we check

  • Business name and address
  • Phone number and email
  • Contact page
  • About page
  • Details match Merchant Center
  • Company registration where relevant

What we often find

  • ! Email address only
  • ! No address anywhere on the site
  • ! Business name differs from the account
  • ! About page with stock text

What we change

  • Full contact details in the footer and contact page
  • Business details that match the account
  • An about page that says who you are
  • Registration number where shoppers expect it

Area 2 of 8

Returns, refunds and shipping

Shoppers need to know what happens if something goes wrong. Google checks that policies exist, are easy to find and match your Merchant Center settings.

What we check

  • Returns and refund policy
  • Shipping costs and times
  • Links from footer and checkout
  • Settings in Merchant Center
  • Policy per country
  • Terms of service

What we often find

  • ! No returns policy at all
  • ! Shipping costs only shown at checkout
  • ! Policies that differ from the settings
  • ! Copied terms naming another store

What we change

  • Clear policies written for your store
  • Linked from the footer and checkout
  • Merchant Center settings that match
  • Terms that name your business

Area 3 of 8

Checkout and payment

Google checks that shoppers can actually buy, and that payment is secure and clear.

What we check

  • Secure checkout
  • Payment methods shown
  • Every product can be bought
  • No surprise costs
  • Checkout on phone
  • Order confirmation

What we often find

  • ! Products in the feed that can’t be bought
  • ! Extra fees added at the last step
  • ! Checkout broken on phone
  • ! Payment methods not shown

What we change

  • Only buyable products in the feed
  • All costs shown before checkout
  • Checkout tested on desktop and phone
  • Payment methods on product pages

Area 4 of 8

Offers and claims

Discounts and claims must be real and easy to check. Permanent sales and unproven claims read as misleading.

What we check

  • Sale banners and dates
  • “Was” prices
  • Claims such as “original” or “certified”
  • Reviews and ratings
  • Free shipping claims
  • Guarantees

What we often find

  • ! A “sale” that never ends
  • ! “Was” prices that were never charged
  • ! Certification claims without proof
  • ! Reviews copied from other sites

What we change

  • Sales with real start and end dates
  • “Was” prices you actually charged
  • Claims removed or backed up
  • Reviews from a real review platform

Area 5 of 8

Prices, stock and product data

The price and stock in your feed must match the site. Repeated mismatches lead to warnings, then a suspension.

What we check

  • Price and sale price
  • Availability and stock
  • Currency
  • Structured data
  • Feed update schedule
  • Automatic item updates

What we often find

  • ! 86 price mismatches in a month
  • ! Sold-out products still in the feed
  • ! Sale prices missing from the feed
  • ! No structured data on product pages

What we change

  • Feed synced several times a day
  • Sale prices with dates
  • Stock synced from the store
  • Structured data on every product page

Area 6 of 8

Restricted products

Some products can’t be shown in Shopping, and some only with rules. A few wrong products can flag the whole account.

What we check

  • Products against Shopping policies
  • Health and medical claims
  • Replicas and counterfeits
  • Weapons and dangerous goods
  • Adult products
  • Country rules

What we often find

  • ! Supplements with health claims
  • ! Products Google doesn’t allow left in the feed
  • ! “Inspired by” replicas
  • ! Titles with banned words

What we change

  • Products excluded from the feed where needed
  • Claims rewritten within the rules
  • Titles and descriptions cleaned
  • A list of products to keep out of Shopping

Area 7 of 8

Website quality

Google expects a finished store: no placeholder text, no dead links, no empty categories.

What we check

  • Placeholder and test text
  • Broken links
  • Empty categories
  • Page speed
  • Images
  • Mobile layout

What we often find

  • ! “Lorem ipsum” on live pages
  • ! 41 broken links
  • ! Empty categories in the menu
  • ! Images that don’t load

What we change

  • Placeholder text removed
  • Broken links fixed
  • Empty categories hidden
  • Images and layout checked on phone

Area 8 of 8

Account and review history

Earlier warnings, refused reviews and linked accounts all shape what Google does next.

What we check

  • Account status and notices
  • Earlier review requests
  • Linked Google Ads accounts
  • Users and access
  • Website claim
  • Other accounts for the same store

What we often find

  • ! Two refused review requests
  • ! A second account opened for the same store
  • ! A former agency still with admin access
  • ! Website claimed by another account

What we change

  • A clear history for the review request
  • One account for the store
  • Access in your name
  • Website claimed by the right account

attrs.title: Why stores get suspended
attrs.lead: The issues behind most suspensions we see, what they look like and how we fix them.

items.title: No business details
items.problem: No address or phone number on the store, so Google can’t tell who is selling.
items.fix: Full contact details in the footer and contact page, matching Merchant Center.

items.title: No clear returns policy
items.problem: Returns are mentioned at checkout, but there’s no policy page, or it’s copied from another store.
items.fix: A clear policy for your store, linked from the footer and checkout, and set in Merchant Center.

items.title: Prices that don’t match
items.problem: The feed shows a different price from the site, often after a sale starts.
items.fix: Feed and store synced several times a day, with structured data on product pages.

items.title: Offers that look too good
items.problem: A permanent sale, “was” prices never charged, or claims with no proof.
items.fix: Real sale dates, honest “was” prices, and claims removed or backed up.

items.title: Restricted products
items.problem: Health claims or products Google doesn’t allow, left in the feed.
items.fix: Products excluded or rewritten within Google’s Shopping policies.

attrs.title: What it’s like to work with us
Merchant Center Suspension Help questions, answered
attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: Why is my Merchant Center suspended for misrepresentation?
items.answer: Google thinks shoppers might be misled, often because of missing business details, unclear policies, prices that don’t match, or offers that look too good to be true.

items.question: How do I fix a Merchant Center suspension?
items.answer: Fix the website and product data first, then request a review. Requesting a review without changes often leads to a cool-down period before you can try again.

items.question: How long does a Merchant Center review take?
items.answer: Usually a few days, sometimes longer. Repeated failed reviews can add waiting time.

items.question: Does a suspension stop free listings too?
items.answer: Yes. A suspended account stops both Shopping ads and free listings, so products disappear from Google Shopping entirely.

items.question: Should I open a new Merchant Center account?
items.answer: No. Opening another account for the same store to get around a suspension breaks Google’s policies and can make things worse.

items.question: Can you guarantee the suspension will be lifted?
items.answer: No. Google makes the decision. We fix the likely causes and request a review once the store is ready.
